title: Programmable Bulk Topological Channels via Strain Engineering
abstract: Accumulated disorder at physical boundaries prevents the realization of ideal zero-dissipation topological edge channels. Here, we propose a strain engineering mechanism to create a topological domain wall in the pristine material bulk, thereby generating interior chiral channels spatially decoupled from physical boundaries. Quantum transport simulations reveal that these interior channels exhibit exceptional immunity to severe boundary disorder, maintaining an ideal vortex-free transport morphology. Furthermore, the spatial position and confinement of these interior channels can be quantitatively programmed. Under a linear gradient strain field, the channel width obeys an inverse square-root scaling law with respect to the strain gradient. In a high-Chern-number phase (|C|=2), we design the spatial splitting and merging of co-propagating chiral channels, suggesting a topological Mach-Zehnder-like geometry. These results suggest a route toward programmable bulk topological transport and reconfigurable topological circuitry.
summary: The paper proposes using controlled strain engineering as a mechanism to create and program robust chiral topological channels deep within the bulk of a material. By inducing internal topological domain walls, these channels bypass the limitations imposed by physical boundaries and disorder. This opens a pathway toward realizing reconfigurable, all-solid-state topological quantum circuitry.
main_problem: Ideal zero-dissipation topological edge channels are hindered by disorder at physical boundaries, necessitating a method to create robust interior chiral channels.
main_result: Strain engineering allows for the creation of topologically protected domain walls in the bulk, generating interior channels immune to boundary disorder and enabling programmable channel geometries like Mach-Zehnder interferometers.
method: The study uses theoretical quantum transport simulations based on tight-binding Hamiltonians modified by controlled mechanical strain fields (gradient strain).
model_or_system: The system is modeled using the Haldane model, realized in ferromagnetic honeycomb insulators. Strain ($\epsilon(y)$) is applied to induce topological domain walls within the bulk material.
key_observables:
Quantized transmission coefficient ($T=1$), channel width scaling ($\sigma \propto 1/\sqrt{

important_parameters: Strain gradient field $\epsilon(y)$, Chern number $|C|$, and disorder strength $W t_1 /$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on continuum approximations for width scaling, and initial models assume constant phases ($\phi$) during lattice deformation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structure evolution under uniform strain, the formation of interior domain walls via gradient strain, robustness against disorder (quantized T), and controlled splitting/recombination circuits in high-Chern-number phases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing uniform strain effects on topological invariants to introducing a continuous linear gradient strain field. This enables the writing of internal domain walls, which are then shown to host robust chiral channels whose properties (width, position) can be quantitatively tuned for circuit design.
why_interesting: This work provides a purely mechanical paradigm for controlling quantum transport features, offering an alternative to lithography or external fields for realizing complex topological circuits relevant to open quantum systems research.
